1.explanation: Both TimePicker and TimePickerSelect render functions compute the CSS class names that drive the layout and heights of the input field and the select boxes. To support 32px and 48px heights you must introduce a new prop (e.g. `size` or specific boolean flags) in both classes’ `propTypes`/`defaultProps` and then augment their `render()` methods so that the computed `className` includes a modifier (for example `${prefix}--time-picker--32` or `${prefix}--time-picker--48`). These modifier classes will target the correct CSS height for the input and select elements. Without touching the render methods and prop definitions here, the component cannot apply the new styles for the extra size variants.
1.bug_scenario: The design adds two new size variants—32px and 48px—for the TimePicker component (in addition to the existing 40px default). The screenshots show three horizontal groups of a text input (“hh:mm”) next to two select menus (“AM” and “Timezone”), each group labeled with its target height: 32px, 40px, and 48px. Currently the component only renders a single fixed height (≈40px), so the 32px and 48px variants do not appear correctly.

2.explanation: To support custom 32px and 48px heights, the TimePicker and TimePickerSelect components must accept a size prop and apply corresponding CSS classes through their render methods. Currently, both components always render with the default 40px height class ("${prefix}--time-picker" and "${prefix}--time-picker__select"). By updating their propTypes/defaultProps to include a size option and modifying the render() methods to conditionally add a `--time-picker--{size}` or `--time-picker__select--{size}` class, the 32px and 48px variants can be styled correctly.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots show three inline time-picker controls labeled as 32px, 40px, and 48px variants. The 40px control displays at the correct height, but the 32px and 48px controls render at the same default height (40px) instead of their intended 32px and 48px sizes. The size variants aren’t being applied to either the input or its accompanying select dropdowns.
